title: Multi-agent tasks: which coding agent
how_to_use: For task class X use classes.X.first_choice; if it cannot run right now, take the next entry in fallbacks. For coding and agentic work, use classes.X.subclasses.Y instead when the task is clearly kind Y.

method.own_success: own_success: a weekly random sample of jobs graded against their own instructions (pass 1, partial 0.5, fail 0) once a pair has enough graded jobs, else the share of jobs that finished cleanly.
method.cost: cost_rank: estimated list-price cost per successful job, cheapest 1, dearest 0 (inverted min-max over log cost across the class's candidates); cheaper wins when quality is close. Estimate from own jobs when a pair has 3 or more successful ones in the class (cost_source 'own jobs'), else the model's blended list price times the engine's typical job size ('list price'), else 0.5 ('default').
method.cost_tier: cost_tier: $ to $$$$, the model's blended list price (3 input : 1 output tokens) in four log-spaced bins from the cheapest to the dearest ranked model. Prices: OpenRouter model list.
method.effort: effort: the reasoning effort to run the entry at. Default: Claude Code Fable medium, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku high; Codex and Grok their CLI config (marked config); Antigravity the -high model id. A public leaderboard that scores the same model at several effort levels moves it only when another level beats the default by at least 0.03 on the class's normalized public score (marked with the source).
method.evidence_rule: Proven means at least 5 own jobs in the window. An unproven entry ranks above a proven one only if its priority is more than 0.03 higher and its public_norm is higher; never on cost or speed alone. Quality before cost: an unproven entry leads only if its public_norm is within 0.05 of the best in the pool.
method.harness_rule: A public metric measured in another agent's harness counts at 0.8x (norm multiplied). The engine's own harness, or a model-only benchmark (no harness or a neutral one), counts in full.
method.subclasses: Coding and agentic subclasses are ranked the same way, on the public metrics that measure that kind of work and own jobs of that kind; a subclass with neither is not listed.

status_meanings.proven: at least 5 own jobs of this kind in the last 28 days
status_meanings.unproven: fewer than 5 own jobs: ranked on public scores
status_meanings.probation: a new version of a model: for its first 28 days it counts its predecessor's own jobs with its own (at least 5 together), and the predecessor's public scores until the leaderboards list it

bugfix.description: finding and fixing defects in existing code

frontend.description: web pages, UI components and styling

multilang.description: repo work outside Python: JS/TS, Go, Rust, Java, PHP

tools.description: multi-step work through APIs and tool connectors

sources.name: Terminal-Bench 4.0
description: Each task gives an agent an instruction and its own environment; the agent works in the terminal, and a verifier's tests decide whether the task was done.
Scored as accuracy over trials, with at least 5 trials per task; errored trials count as failures, and an LLM judge reviews successful trials for reward hacking.
A submission is one agent harness, model and reasoning effort together, so a score says as much about the harness as the model; we count a score from another agent's harness at 0.8x.

sources.name: SWE-bench Verified
description: A model, inside an agent scaffold, gets a GitHub issue and its repository and has to produce a patch that fixes it.
Scored as the percentage of tasks resolved, out of 500 SWE-bench tasks that human annotators checked for clear problem statements and correct tests.
The standard test for fixing bugs in existing code. Caveat: entries are a model plus a scaffold, and the board had no recent entries for most models we rank.

sources.name: SWE-bench Multilingual
sources.measures: repo issues resolved in nine languages
description: SWE-bench-style tasks in other languages: 300 tasks from 42 repositories in C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, Ruby and Rust.
A task counts as resolved when the patch passes two sets of unit tests taken from the original pull request.
Would tell us about repo work outside Python. Caveat: none of the models we rank has an entry yet, so it affects no ranking today.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis coding index
description: A single coding score per model that Artificial Analysis publishes in its API, from its own runs of coding evaluations.
Its methodology page does not list which evaluations make up this index, so we do not describe its parts.
Not in use: the API needs a key we do not use, so no model has a value here.
sources.note: not fetched: the source needs an API key we do not use

sources.name: Arena Text: coding
description: People ask a question in Arena's battle mode, see answers from two anonymous models side by side and vote for the better one; this board keeps only prompts Arena classifies as coding.
Ratings come from a Bradley-Terry fit to those votes, published as the Arena score.
Shows whose coding answers people prefer in chat. Caveat: preference in a chat answer, not whether the code runs in a repository.

sources.name: Arena WebDev
sources.measures: people's votes on built web apps
description: Code Arena: two anonymous models build a web app or page from the same request and people vote on the result; Arena describes it as full-stack web development with multi-step reasoning, tool use and end-to-end app generation.
Rated from the votes and published as the Arena score; one model can appear at two reasoning efforts.
Our best signal for frontend and UI work. Caveat: it judges the finished app as people see it, not the code behind it.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis agentic index
description: A single agentic score per model that Artificial Analysis publishes in its API.
Its methodology page does not list which evaluations make up this index, so we do not describe its parts.
Not in use: the API needs a key we do not use, so no model has a value here.
sources.note: not fetched: the source needs an API key we do not use

sources.name: Arena Agent: bash reliability
sources.measures: shell work in real agent sessions
description: A shell-command signal from Agent Arena, which analyses real sessions of people using Agent Mode on arena.ai for their own work.
Published as an IPS score with a 95% confidence interval; Arena's methodology post does not define this particular signal, so we do not describe how it is counted.
Feeds terminal and sysadmin work. Caveat: the sessions run in Arena's own agent, on whatever tasks its users bring.

sources.name: Arena Agent: bash recovery
sources.measures: recovering from a failed shell command
description: After a shell command errors in a real Agent Mode session, how many more turns the agent takes to reach a command that runs; giving up is penalised.
Published as an IPS score with a 95% confidence interval.
Feeds terminal and sysadmin work. Caveat: measured in Arena's own agent, on its users' tasks.

sources.name: Arena Agent: tool calls
sources.measures: not calling tools that do not exist
description: In real Agent Mode sessions, a task is marked a failure when the agent calls a tool that does not exist.
Published as an IPS score with a 95% confidence interval; the spread between models is small.
Feeds tool and connector workflows. Caveat: it catches invented tools, not wrong arguments to real ones.

sources.name: Arena Agent: task outcome
description: At the end of a real Agent Mode session the user marks the task a success or a failure in Arena's interface.
Published as an IPS score with a 95% confidence interval.
Feeds tool and connector workflows. Caveat: each user judges their own task, in Arena's agent.

sources.name: DeepResearch Bench
description: 100 PhD-level research tasks (50 in Chinese, 50 in English) across 22 fields, written by domain experts; a system writes a full research report for each.
Reports are judged by RACE, which compares them with reference reports using an LLM judge, and FACT, which checks how many citations are effective and accurate; we read the leaderboard's total score.
Would tell us about deep research. Caveat: most entries are research products, not the models we rank, and none of ours has an entry.

sources.name: Arena Search
description: Arena's leaderboard for searching the web: people compare two anonymous models' answers side by side and vote.
Rated with a Bradley-Terry fit to the votes, published as the Arena score.
Feeds research. Caveat: few of the models we rank have an entry.

sources.name: Arena Document
sources.measures: people's votes on answers about PDFs
description: People upload a PDF, ask about it, and compare two anonymous models' answers side by side.
Rated with a Bradley-Terry fit to the votes, published as the Arena score.
Feeds reading. Caveat: questions about one uploaded document, not reading across many files.

sources.name: Arena Text: creative writing
description: Arena Text battles in the creative writing category: two anonymous answers, and people vote for the one they prefer.
Rated with a Bradley-Terry fit to the votes, published as the Arena score.
Feeds writing. Caveat: taste in short chat answers; it says nothing about long documents or a house style.

sources.name: Arena Text
sources.measures: people's votes on all text prompts
description: All Arena Text battles: people see answers from two anonymous models side by side and vote for the better one.
Rated with a Bradley-Terry fit to the votes, published as the Arena score; we use the raw ratings, not the style-controlled ones.
Feeds writing as a general quality signal. Caveat: a broad mix of everyday prompts, specific to no one task.

sources.name: Artificial Analysis output speed
description: How fast a model streams its answer: tokens received per second after the first token, measured on the same endpoint Artificial Analysis uses for price.
Higher is faster; we would scale it across the models we rank.
Only a fallback when we have no timings of our own. Not in use: the API needs a key we do not use.
sources.note: not fetched: the source needs an API key we do not use

sources.name: OpenRouter prices
description: The per-token prices OpenRouter lists for each model, taken from the top provider for that model, in US dollars.
We blend 3 input tokens to 1 output token and show dollars per million tokens; lower is cheaper.
Sets the $ to $$$$ tier, and the cost estimate when we have fewer than 3 priced jobs of our own. Caveat: one provider's list price, which can differ from the model maker's own price.

sources.name: Own jobs
sources.measures: our own dispatched jobs over 28 days
description: The jobs we hand to these agents in our own work, counted per engine and model for each task class and kind.

Own success is the share that finished cleanly or, once a pair has enough graded jobs, the mean grade from a weekly random sample graded against each job's own instructions; median minutes and list-price cost also count.
Only aggregate counts and rates are published, never the jobs themselves. Caveat: our own task mix, not a general benchmark.
